title: Masters of the Air: America's Bomber Boys Who Fought the Air War Against Nazi Germany
author: Donald L. Miller
note: Selected for historian Richard B. Frank's praise, aviation historian Walter J. Boyne's endorsement and Goodreads 4.22/10,668. Endorsements are reproduced on the author's university website, not independent full reviews. Publishers Weekly provides a separate favorable assessment that also identifies the limits of strategic bombing claims. Military history is central, so T12 applies. Although American airmen frame the narrative, its central consequences concern German industry and the international war; T11=0. Operational learning, doctrine, technology and industrial targeting provide transferable payload. No serious veto established from inspected evidence.
notes: Archival research, diaries and oral histories support the account; retrospective testimony requires caution.
Connects aviation technology, doctrine, industrial targets, logistics and human limits.
Useful lessons on testing doctrine against operational evidence and adapting organizations.
Explains the gap between bombing claims and operational constraints.
